It was played on 15 May 2024 between [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] and [[Juventus FC|Juventus]].{{cite web |last1=Bonn |first1=Kyle |title=How to watch Coppa Italia in USA: 2023/24 Italian league Cup on Paramount+ from Serie A broadcaster CBS |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/soccer/news/watch-coppa-italia-usa-2023-2024-league-cup-paramount-cbs/1bcbe1ac51e7948952fb1beb |website=[[The Sporting News]] |language=en-us |date=11 January 2024}}{{cite web |title=Coppa Italia 2024 TV Schedule USA and Streaming Links |url=https://worldsoccertalk.com/coppa-italia-tv-schedule-and-streaming-links/ |website=World Soccer Talk |date=4 January 2021 |access-date=25 April 2024 |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240425172021/https://worldsoccertalk.com/coppa-italia-tv-schedule-and-streaming-links/ |archive-date=25 April 2024 |url-status=live}} Juventus won the match 1–0 for a record-extending 15th Coppa Italia title.{{cite web|url=https://www.legaseriea.it/en/media/coppa-italia/juventus-lift-the-15th-coppa-italia-13jgek51a3n73b|title=Juventus lift their 15th Coppa Italia|publisher=[[Lega Serie A]]|date=15 May 2024|access-date=15 May 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cxwvzr31yrvt |title= Atalanta 0 Juventus 1|date=15 May 2024|work=BBC Sport |accessdate=16 May 2024}} == Background == Atalanta had previously played in five Coppa Italia finals, winning once. Their most recent final appearance was in [[2021 Coppa Italia final|2021]] a 2–1 defeat to Juventus; their only win was in [[1963 Coppa Italia final|1963]], a 3–1 victory over [[Torino FC|Torino]], which was also their most recent major title. Juventus had won 14 of their 21 appearances in the cup final. Their most recent appearance was a 4–2 [[Overtime (sports)#association football|extra time]] loss to [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] in [[2022 Coppa Italia final|2022]]. The two teams had last met in the Coppa Italia final in 2021, where Juventus won 2–1. That was also Juventus' most recent win in the cup. This win marked the last trophy of the [[Massimiliano Allegri]] managerial era in Juventus, as he got sacked two days later, on 17 May 2024.{{cite web|title=Massimiliano Allegri's legacy at Juventus|date= 20 May 2024|work=CBS Sports |url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/massimiliano-allegris-legacy-at-juventus-why-his-second-stint-at-the-club-ended-in-turbulent-failure/ |accessdate=2 July 2025}} In reaching the final, both teams qualified for the [[2024–25 Supercoppa Italiana]] (for the first time in Atalanta's case). ==Road to the final== ''Note: In all results below, the score of the finalist is given first (H: home; A: away).'' {| width="100%" style="text-align:center" |- valign=top bgcolor=#99ccff !colspan=2 style="width:40%"|[[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] !Round !colspan=2 style="width:40%"|[[Juventus FC|Juventus]] |- valign=top bgcolor=#c1e0ff |Opponent |Result |bgcolor=#c1e0ff|[[2023–24 Coppa Italia]] |Opponent |Result |- |[[US Sassuolo Calcio|Sassuolo]] |3–1 |bgcolor=#c1e0ff|Round of 16 |[[US Salernitana 1919|Salernitana]] |6–1 |- |[[AC Milan|Milan]] |2–1 |bgcolor=#c1e0ff|Quarter-finals |[[Frosinone Calcio|Frosinone]] |4–0 |- |[[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] |0–1 (A), 4–1 (H)

{{agg|3–2}} |} == Match == === Summary === The game started in front of 66,854 people. In the fourth minute, [[Andrea Cambiaso]] sent an elevated through ball to [[Dušan Vlahović]], who ran into the box and scored a goal past [[Marco Carnesecchi]] from around the penalty spot.{{Cite web |title=Juventus V.S Atalanta Timeline – Google Sport |url=https://www.google.com/search?q=juventus+atalanta&safe=active#sie=m;/g/11y1r1qkp8;2;/m/04psgg;dt;fp;1;;; |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=www.google.com}}{{Cite web |title=Atalanta 1–0 Juventus (16 May, 2024) Game Analysis – ESPN (AU) |url=http://www.espn.com.au/football/report/_/gameId/702196 |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=ESPN |language=en}}{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xzdnvFuPqqQ |title=Atalanta–Juventus 0–1 {{!}} Highlights {{!}} Vlahovic wins it for Juve! {{!}} Coppa Italia Frecciarossa 2023/24 |date=2024-05-15 |last=Serie A |access-date=2024-05-16 |via=YouTube}} In the eighth minute, [[Hans Nicolussi Caviglia]] sent a corner into the box which [[Weston McKennie]] headed into [[Federico Gatti]], who headed over the crossbar. In the seventeenth minute, [[Isak Hien]] was shown a [[Yellow card (football)|yellow card]] for knocking down [[Federico Chiesa]]. In the forty-fifth minute, [[Mario Pašalić]] sent in a ball from just inside the box from a build-up from a corner, which hit McKennie on its way before Gatti deflected the shot. At halftime, [[Charles De Ketelaere]] was taken off in replacement for [[El Bilal Touré]]. In the fifty-fifth minute, Vlahović had a clear run to the goal but was taken down by Hien on the [[Byline (association football)|byline]]. No penalty was called by the referee, but after dissent, Vlahović was shown a yellow card. In the fifty-ninth minute, Atalanta made a triple sub, putting on [[Hans Hateboer]], [[Giorgio Scalvini]] and [[Aleksei Miranchuk]] for Hien, [[Mario Pašalić]] and [[Davide Zappacosta]]. Three minutes later, Juventus brought on [[Fabio Miretti]] for Nicolussi Caviglia. Shortly after, they made a sub for Chiesa, bringing on young talent [[Kenan Yıldız]]. In the seventy-second minute, Cambiaso sendt in a cross to Vlahović from outside the box, where he headed it in for a goal. However, after a [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] check, Vlahović was identified as offside. After six minutes of [[injury time]] and a [[Red card (sport)|red card]] shown to coach [[Massimiliano Allegri]], the game was finished as Juventus won their record extending 15th Coppa Italia. ===
